title: Deterministic multi-node throughput regression harness for tensor+pipeline parallel models
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic, CI-friendly load test harness that measures end-to-end tokens/sec and latency p95 across multi-node, tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel model shards, and enforces automatic regression detection based on baseline snapshots.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Harness runs stable synthetic workloads that emulate production token length distributions and prompt mixes (instruct/chat/streaming).
- Measure and persist per-run metrics: tokens/sec (global and per-GPU), p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, KV-cache hit ratio, memory headroom, NCCL retry counts, and GPU SM utilization.
- Support config matrix: nodes {1,2,4,8,16}, GPUs/node {1,4,8}, tensor-parallel sizes {1,2,4}, pipeline-parallel stages {1,2,4,8}, micro-batch sizes, and KV-cache warm vs cold.
- Deterministic RNG seeds and fixed prompt corpus to make results reproducible across runs and CI.
- Snapshot baseline storage (S3) and a regression detector that compares a new run to the latest baseline and fails CI if tokens/sec drops >5% or p95 increases >10%. Thresholds configurable per-model and per-release.
- Integrate with CI: add a `perf-check` job that can be toggled per-PR or run nightly for release branches.
- Produce human-readable report and linkable Grafana dashboards and raw JSON artifacts for debugging.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Synthetic vs production traces: synthetic corpora let us be deterministic and fast but may miss correlated tail behavior observed in production. We'll provide a mode that replays sampled production traces (anonymized) for nightly regression runs.
- Cost vs coverage: full matrix across nodes/parallelism is expensive. CI will run a minimal smoke configuration; nightly release jobs will run expanded matrix.
- Deterministic NCCL behavior across different kernel builds can vary; harness will pin driver/runtime versions and log environment details to make baseline comparisons meaningful.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Harness core: executor that launches distributed model servers (k8s or on-instance runner) and coordinates clients to feed requests at target QPS while measuring latencies. (Owner: Maya)
2) Metric collector: central process that aggregates per-GPU telemetry via DCGM and perf counters, merges with client-side latencies, stores combined JSON to S3 and pushes curated metrics to Grafana. (Owner: Priya Rao)
3) Deterministic workload generator: corpus and runner with seeded RNG, tokenization determinism, and KV-cache warmup scripts. (Owner: Alex Li)
4) Regression detector and CI integration: snapshot management, comparison logic, PR comment automation, and gating rules. (Owner: Ethan)
5) Dashboarding and reporting: Grafana panels for tokens/sec heatmaps, p95 contours, and a human report generator. (Owner: DataInfra team)

Milestones:
- 2025-01-31: Core harness prototype that runs a 2-node tensor-parallel test and stores artifacts.
- 2025-02-10: Metric collector and baseline snapshot tool complete; first nightly expanded matrix run.
- 2025-02-20: Regression detector and CI gate prototype merged; docs and runbook published.

Notes on measurement methodology:
- Tokens/sec: measure both client-observed emitted tokens/sec and server-side decoded token counts to detect discrepancies due to truncation or early stopping.
- Latency measurements: include client-side ingress->egress p50/p95/p99 and server-side decode-step timing when available to isolate kernel vs scheduling delays.
- Warm vs cold KV-cache: run each config with a short warmup phase (10k tokens) and a cold phase, and store both results.
- Statistical significance: for tight thresholds, run multiple iterations and compute median and interquartile ranges; regression detector will use bootstrap sampling for confidence intervals.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/DT-986/harness-design
- Reference harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness (branch: eng/ENG-14285)
- Example baseline artifact: s3://redwood-perf/baselines/eng-14285/runtime-1.20/2025-01-28.json
- Grafana dashboard (perf/dev): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/throughput/multi-node-throughput

Operational concerns:
- We must ensure harness cannot overload shared staging clusters; provide a dedicated perf namespace and quota.
- Baseline drift: record environment metadata (driver, CUDA, kernel versions, model checksum) and include as part of the snapshot to avoid comparing incompatible runs.

Risks and mitigation:
- Non-determinism from NCCL and scheduler jitter: mitigate by pinning versions, building a stable kernel image for perf runs, and using retries/aggregation.
- CI noise: to avoid false positives, CI will run a lightweight smoke check and require manual triage for larger diffs; regression gating only triggers on release-nightly jobs by default.

Acceptance criteria (done):
- Prototype run reproducible on a different machine with the same pinned image and returns tokens/sec within 2% of baseline.
- Regression detector raises actionable alerts with diff summary and links to raw artifacts.
- Runbook published and a demo completed with Platform and Reliability stakeholders.
